channel.title: Lucas Wetzel
channel.description: Lucas Wetzel — theoretical physics. Self-organized synchronization in networks of delay-coupled oscillators, from segmentation clocks to phase-locked loops.

item.title: Control theory of mutual synchronization in networks of delay-coupled phase-locked loops
item.description: Gain and phase margins assume an entraining reference. Mutual coupling changes the transfer function itself.

item.title: Ising Machines
item.description: Mapping combinatorial optimisation onto networks of coupled oscillators, and what sub-harmonic injection locking, inertia and delay do to the answer.

item.title: Synchronization of rhythm in human human, human machine and machine machine interactions
item.description: What a room full of people clapping and a network of clocks have in common, and where the analogy stops.

item.title: On the differences between universal emergent time (UEC) and universal coordinated time (UTC)
item.description: Today's time standards feed a reference forward. What would a standard look like if the reference emerged from the network instead?

item.title: Howto run independent voltage noise sources (IID and GWN) in LTSpice using Bv-sources
item.description: LTSpice has no built-in noise source for transient runs. Bv-sources with white() get you independent, band-limited Gaussian noise.

item.title: Spice simulation of self-organized synchronization with LTC6900 oscillators
item.description: Two mutually delay-coupled DPLLs at 1 MHz in LTspice, and how the circuit parameters map onto the phase model.

item.title: Science Slam @Elbhangfest in Dresden, 2018/06/23
item.description: Ask an audience to clap for an encore and they synchronize. Ask them to do it a billion times a second and you need a different idea. (English and German)

item.title: Spice simulations of digital phase-locked loop systems
item.description: Testing DPLL architectures down to the transistor level before soldering anything.

item.title: Self-organized synchronization in electronic systems
item.description: The concept, the phase model, the prototype network, and what happens when clocks are heterogeneous.
